analysis:
This PR changes only documentation: a new changelog.d/glm53-native-prerequisites.md and docs/architecture/hardware-support.md. No source was supplied, so the code claims made in the docs are unverified. No concrete regression is visible in the text.

Security-relevant behavior the docs describe, for the next pass to check against code:
- GLM-5.3-Flash is served in coordinator mode as `glm-5.3-flash`. The provider self-reports runtime capability `glm5_next_v1` on M5 Max/Ultra with at least 256 GB. Platform routing must not treat this self-reported capability as proof of hardware or build identity; it needs attestation or qualification (TB-002, TB-011, T-054).
- The GLM encrypted SSD prefix store is default-on for the pinned GLM identity, with `DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE=0` as the opt-out. This falls under T-041/SEC-035. The 30-minute TTL, HMAC-keyed names and coordinator-authored cacheSalt must still apply to the GLM paths (embedded MTP, rectangular verify, paged KV). Image rows are said never to reuse cached prefixes, which is good. Verify that the GLM identity and checkpoint policy are bound into the DBK3 AAD and layoutEpoch.
- Media: images are decrypted and prepared natively in-process. Video is refused. Confirm that no temp-file path exists (cf. T-050) and that the image-media reservation bounds (pixels, 8000-token cap) hold against consumer-driven memory DoS.
- Memory admission: the raw-source-size quotation replaces disk x1.2 using `ceil(source/32)`. Check the metadata-only directory discovery and the refusal of symlinks and nested integrity files (TB-003, T-012 weight tampering). The reviewed-template and manifest/aggregate pinning should be mandatory.
- Retained-fault handling (unproven retirement keeps its lease and is excluded from fleet KV grants) affects availability. Local metrics expose `darkbloom_glm5_next_retained_*`. Confirm those metrics leak no tenant data.
- `DARKBLOOM_GLM_RECTANGULAR_VERIFY` is forwarded to the launchd job. Verify the env allowlist.
- hardware-support.md now documents per-request MTP context binding, so a reused request ID cannot revive a retired context. Check AdmissionV2.detachReservation and AdmittedMTPBinding.
- MTP output is not token-identical to target-only greedy decoding (output integrity, T-007 context).

The threat model has no GLM-specific entry. A possible follow-up is to note GLM under T-041 and T-056.
